answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks that require counterparties to stake funds and later attest that the work was useful; repeated attestations from the same cluster count less, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply influence by spawning identities. To gain weight, a sybil attacker must forge convincing work and lock real capital at risk across many independent interactions. The ridge of diminishing returns makes each new identity costlier, while honest agents can wander into new partnerships without needing a central identity issuer.
